name: Aranadan
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Dravidian tribal variety of Kerala; only demographic/anthropological references found (Kakkoth 2004, People of India); no phonological description located

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page aran1261 and the held hh.bib (Glottolog bibliography): descriptive refs for aran1261 are all 'overview' (Menon et al. 2002; Thurston 1909; Menon 1996; Luiz 1962; Fuchs 1973; Reddy 2006; Ramaiah & Reddy 2005; Shashi 1994) plus Nair 2013 (overview;minimal); Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology. hh.bib notes explicitly that Panikkar 1967/1973 'Ernad dialect' is the Muslim (Mappila) dialect of Malayalam, NOT the hunting-gathering Aranadan.
sources.note: No grammar, phonology or sketch is recorded for Aranadan; the only language-focused item is Nair 2013 (examined above). Do not confuse with Panikkar's 'Ernad dialect' of Malayalam (mal).

sources.citation: People's Linguistic Survey of India, Kerala and Lakshadweep volume, Hindi translation (Bharatiya Bhasha Lok Sarvekshan: Kerala aur Lakshadweep ki Bhashayen), tr. Vijayakumaran C.P.V; archive.org item kerala-plsi-24-december-2024-final.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Aranadan chapter. Aranadan (अरनाडन) is named only twice, in the tribal-languages overview: listed as definitely endangered and as conventionally (and, the author says, arbitrarily) treated as a Malayalam dialect. No stress statement for Aranadan.

sources.citation: Robert, Sam. 2019. Linguistic and Cultural Shifts of the Aranadan Tribe in Kerala. The CALA 2019 Proceedings, paper 10-3, pp. 341-346. The GLOCAL, SOAS University of London. doi:10.47298/cala2019.10-3
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic paper on language shift; 'Illustrations of Language Shift' (pp. 344-345) lists segmental changes toward Malayalam (medial long vowel shortening ulaakke > ulakka, final -ai > -e > -a, b > v, e > a), morphological and lexical replacements. No stress/accent/intonation remark; references are ethnographic plus Usha 1992 kinship working paper.

sources.citation: Nair, Ravi Sankar S. 2013. Tribal Languages of Kerala. Language in India 13(7): 1-58 (Aranadan sketch pp. 8-10). Glottolog ref 320019 (overview;minimal).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Aranadan sketch (pp. 8-10) lists segmental features only (vowel nasalization, medial vowel lengthening, final -a > -e, v > b, l > y/j, rr > cc), pronouns, plural, case deletion, tense suffixes and a few lexical items; the words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the document.

sources.citation: Menon, T. Madhava (chief ed.) and M. Sasikumar (asst. ed.). 1996. The Encyclopaedia of Dravidian Tribes, Vol. II. Thiruvananthapuram: International School of Dravidian Linguistics. Entry 'Aranadan Language' (unsigned; scan leaves 22-23, printed page not recoverable from scanned). Glottolog ref 305507.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Aranadan Language' entry gives the same segmental and morphological notes as Nair 2013 (nasalization, vowel lengthening, -a > -e, v > b, l > y/j, rr > cc, plural -kal, dative/genitive deletion, tense suffixes) plus kinship terms; no mention of stress, accent or intonation. a full-text search for stress/accent/'accent' in the whole volume hits only other tribes ('speak Telugu with a peculiar accent').

sources.citation: Thurston, Edgar and K. Rangachari. 1909. Castes and Tribes of Southern India, Vol. II, entry 'Ernadan' pp. 217-218 (Vol. I index: 'Aranadan, see Ernadan'). Madras: Government Press. Glottolog ref 99321.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic only (python-oil trade, pollution distance, bows and arrows, anthropometry); nothing about the language at all.

sources.note: No thesis on Aranadan exists in Shodhganga. Kerala tribal-language theses found are on Kattunayaka, Malaveda, Muduga only. Sam Robert's Shodhganga thesis (2023) is on English-language learning, not Aranadan.
